source_text: Sed insertis aliis verbis meis, ubi voluntatem vere piorum, quia Christianorum, coniugum commendavi, qui filios ad hoc generant in hoc saeculo, ut propter alterum saeculum regenerentur in Christo … commemoras te iam in secundo libro istam meam destruxisse sententiam
pass_a_gloss: But other words of mine having been inserted, where I commended the will of truly pious, because Christian, spouses, who generate sons to this end in this age, that on account of the other age they may be regenerated in Christ; you mention that you already in the second book destroyed this opinion of mine.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “But you insert other words of mine, where I commended the will of spouses who are truly devout because they are Christians, who beget children in this age for this purpose, that they may be reborn in Christ for the sake of the other age. Then you mention that you already demolished this view of mine in your second book.”

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
